newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas called steady, cash still firm.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas called steady, cash still firm.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures were expected to open little changed Monday amid early talk of firm cash prices coupled with cooler weather stretching across most of the U.S., industry sources said.
September over-the-counter trade ranged from $2.22 to $2.24, with a deal reported done at 0930 EDT at $2.23. It settled to the upside Friday at $2.239 per million British thermal units.
Early cash prices at Henry Hub were talked steady to slightly stronger at $2.23-2.255 due to the uptick in cooling demand in California, traders said.
Technical traders said September support was at $2.20-2.205 and then at $2.15-2.16 and $2.08. Resistance was pegged at $2.27 and then at $2.325-2.33.
In Friday's cash, Gulf Coast gas was steady to up slightly at $2.20. Midcon pipes showed similar movement to the mid-teens. New York city gate prices also were moved higher to the mid-$2.40s.

Cooler-than-normal temperatures are expected to cover most of the U.S. early this week, with readings of about five to 10 degrees F below normal forecast for the Mid-Atlantic states through Wednesday, Weather Services Corp said. However, above-normal temperatures continued over parts of California and Arizona, with highs expected to hover around 100 degrees F over the next few days in Sacramento, Calif.
